newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan 1997 exports, imports seen rising 8.0 pct.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan 1997 exports, imports seen rising 8.0 pct.

text.p: Taiwan's imports and exports both will rise by over eight percent in 1997 compared with 1996, a Finance Ministry director said on Tuesday, quoting official projections.
"We expect moderate growth in exports and imports in 1997, each with more than eight percent rise from 1996," ministry director Hsu Kuo-chung told journalists.
An international economic recovery would help exports while the speeding execution of state projects at home would stimulate imports for raw materials, Hsu added.
"The growth of exports should be higher than that of imports," he said without elaborating.
In 1996, Taiwan's exports grew 3.9 percent from 1995 to US$115.98 billion while imports fell 2.2 percent to T$101.28 billion.
